Section 498A and Section 352 of the IPC address specific aspects of domestic violence.Understanding the Sections:Section 498A IPC:Objective: To protect married women from cruelty by their husbands and in-laws.Definition: It covers any willful conduct that is likely to drive a woman to suicide or cause grave injury to her life, limb, or health (whether mental or physical). It also includes harassment with the aim of coercing her or her relatives to meet any unlawful demand for property or valuable security.Punishment: Imprisonment for up to three years and a fine.Section 352 IPC:Objective: To address assault or use of criminal force otherwise than on grave provocation.Definition: It penalizes the act of assault or use of criminal force against any person without grave and sudden provocation by that person.Punishment: Imprisonment for up to three months, or a fine of up to five hundred rupees, or both.Determining the Applicability:Section 498A: If the case involves a married woman being subjected to cruelty by her husband or in-laws, particularly with respect to harassment for dowry or inflicting harm that could cause serious mental or physical trauma, then it falls under Section 498A.Section 352: If the situation involves an incident where assault or use of criminal force occurred without grave provocation but does not fit the specific criteria of cruelty in a matrimonial context as described in Section 498A, it might fall under Section 352.
